name: ANSI/IEEE thermometer/pyrometer symbol
summary: IEEE-library thermometer/pyrometer form for high-temperature indication, often from thermocouples or radiation sensors.
description: Pyrometer indication is used where temperatures are too high for ordinary thermometers, such as furnaces, kilns and exhaust gas. The instrument is commonly fed from a thermocouple or an optical radiation sensor, so the input wiring and any cold-junction compensation must be shown with the instrument.

The form identifies the indicating instrument, not the sensing principle. A radiation pyrometer and a thermocouple pyrometer look the same at the instrument circle, and emissivity settings or sensor range limits must come from the instrument data.
readingNotes: Identify the sensing element feeding the pyrometer.
Check for cold-junction compensation when a thermocouple is used.
distinction: The pyrometer form signals a high-temperature indicator; the general thermometer form covers ordinary temperature indication.
